title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 344
paragraphs: After him, they said, Mykerinos became king over Egypt — the son of Cheops. His father's deeds displeased him, and he both opened the temples and gave the people, who had been ground down to the last extremity of misery, their liberty to return to their own affairs and to their sacrifices. He also handed down judgments in their lawsuits that were more just than those of all the other kings. For this reason the Egyptians praise this king above all the kings who had arisen in Egypt before him; for he not only gave good decisions, but also, when a man complained of a decision, he paid him compensation out of his own property and so satisfied his desire. But while Mykerinos was acting mercifully to his subjects and conducting himself in the way I have described, calamities befell him. The first was this: his daughter died, the only child he had in his house. Grieved beyond measure by what had happened, and wishing to bury his daughter in a more remarkable manner than others, he made a cow of wood, covered it over with gold, and then buried within it this daughter who, as I said, had died.
